C09122808300.summary: Tamura to Fukushima, Feb 1901: Kamio's (unidentified kekō) is not permitted, and the General Staff means to send him to Himeji.
C09122808300.en:
Kamio's 〔kekō〕 is not permitted; we intend to send him to Himeji.

(Translation after Harumi-Matsuba, READING1901B.en.md; [nn] = value not in the table.)

C09122808400.summary: Tamura to Fukushima, 14 Feb 1901: the matter of Ōshima is under discussion; if he cannot go, how about Kusunose; Shiba will be sent back in any case.
C09122808400.en:
The matter of Ōshima is under discussion now. If he cannot go, how about Kusunose? Shiba will be sent back in any case. Tamura.

(Translation after Harumi-Matsuba, READING1901B.en.md; [nn] = value not in the table.)

C09122809400.summary: Tamura to Fukushima, 2 Mar 1901: Li Hongzhang's answer to Japanese advice against a secret agreement, Zhang Zhidong's request that the treaty should not come into being, and a telegram of the same sense from Xi'an; four word codes unread.
C09122809400.en:
... to our advice that the ... secret agreement is disadvantageous, Li Hongzhang had [60][80] tell [59] that, [99][60] ... considering it advantageous at present ..., the advice is hard to accept .... Also, Zhang Zhidong has asked our [59] that this treaty should not come into being. Also a telegram of the same meaning has come from Xi'an. Tamura.

(Translation after Harumi-Matsuba, READING1901B.en.md; [nn] = value not in the table.)

C09122810100.summary: Tamura to Fukushima, 8 Mar 1901: the Field Marshal (Waldersee, per the contributor) wishes to come to Japan from Kiaochow Bay; Tokyo is sounding out how he would be received and asks Fukushima to recommend the trip if it looks favourable.
C09122810100.en:
The Field Marshal wishes to come to Japan from Kiaochow Bay .... We are sounding out how 〔...〕[89][80] would be placed to receive him. If it looks as though we shall receive him suitably, recommend the 〔pleasure〕 trip to him. Tamura.

(Translation after Harumi-Matsuba, READING1901B.en.md; [nn] = value not in the table.)

C09122812300.summary: Tamura to Fukushima, 1 May 1901: someone is to return home; the number of relief troops cannot be met until a matter (word code 80) is settled.
C09122812300.en:
... is to return home. Also, the number of relief troops: unless [80] is settled, the wish is hard to meet. Tamura.

(Translation after Harumi-Matsuba, READING1901B.en.md; [nn] = value not in the table.)

system: Sensitive words of romanised telegrams put into two-digit kana values on a grid (tens = vowel row, units = consonant column), written in groups of five, with a few off-grid values that look like word codes.
